STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel is a square white plate with a flat centre and a raised rim band. No curved inner wall is visible, so it is a flat plate (square).

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: square plates are 20-30 cm. The plate looks like a standard dinner-sized square, so about 25 cm.
b) Reference cue: the blackberry-like berry is about 2.2 cm across. The plate spans roughly 11-12 of these across its width (about 26 cm of the image frame, with the berry filling roughly 1/11 of the width), giving about 24-26 cm.
Reconciled width: about 25 cm. Area = 625 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Greens/salad (wilted leafy greens with dressing and some red pepper bits): covers about 18% of the plate, about 112 cm². Thickness is a loose mound, about 3 cm average (about 5 cm peak). Volume = 112 × 3 = 336 ml. Cooked leafy greens at 0.6 g/ml gives about 200 g. (Dressing and oil included in this estimate.)
- Hash brown / shredded fried potato (golden, crispy strands): covers about 22% of the plate, about 137 cm². Mound thickness about 2 cm average (about 4 cm peak), so volume about 274 ml × 0.8 (grain/shredded density) ≈ 220 g.
- Single blackberry: 1 berry, about 5 g (chopped fruit density, roughly one berry worth).
- Small leafy/vegetable bit beside the berry: included in the greens estimate.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: The potato base sits beneath and partly under the greens, already counted. No additional hidden layer is evident. The plate is not heaped beyond the mound estimates.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served, cooked):
- Cooked mixed greens with dressing: about 60 kcal/100 g (oil and dressing raise it).
- Fried shredded potato (hash brown): about 200 kcal/100 g (oil absorbed during frying).
- Blackberry: about 45 kcal/100 g.

Totals: greens 200 g → 120 kcal; potato 220 g → 440 kcal; blackberry 5 g → 2 kcal. Overall about 425 g and about 560 kcal.
